threshold_origin: The print bound was chosen on these development renders: plain tops scored 0.11 to 0.42 of the bought blouse's edge detail and patterned tops 0.50 to 0.70. The stability box and pixel threshold are the held-out study's frozen values. This report is therefore not an unseen test of the gate.

limits: Print busyness is mean edge strength inside the garment area; it is not a judgement of taste or a pattern classifier.
The stability measurement uses a fixed garment band; hands, hair and shadows inside the band are not checked.
Sleeves and neckline are not measured; they remain catalog facts.
A verdict of shows means the three measurements agree with the request; it does not establish fit, fabric or exact colour.

Colour is compared with the catalog colour without correcting for the light in the photo. In gate-study-v2 the blind AI rater accepted all ten renders the colour check flagged, allowing for the photo's lighting.
Print busyness also counts construction detail. The utility shirt's pockets, buttons and seams read as not quieter on all four new photos, where the blind AI rater saw a plain shirt.

The two patterned sweaters registered as tops that should fail were weak negatives: a yoke band and broad stripes are less busy than the dense floral, and the blind AI rater judged all eight quieter. A live test against a top as busy as the blouse is still to be run.
On the full-length photo Clothes V4 also redrew trousers and waistlines in some renders; the stability band flagged seven of its eight renders, at 3.0 to 4.5 percent, including the blouse itself.
The protocol named the owner as a second, human rater; the owner chose not to label, so only the AI rater is reported.
